clue.text: From hotel bar, you can see the whole island

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the words hotel bar, so this signals a run concealed inside them

explanation.surface: From the hotel bar there is a view across the entire island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' signals letters lifted out of 'hotel bar'; 'you can see the whole' is a playful link saying the island is in plain view.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is the Mediterranean island off Tuscany where Napoleon was exiled.

clue.text: Steps taken to make an apology?

definitions.meaning: a dance in which one partner may cut in on another couple
the phrase said when apologising for a small intrusion

explanation.surface: Someone takes careful steps towards saying sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: The polite formula for apologising doubles as the name of a ballroom dance with partner changes.

clue.text: Scottish area enrolling a group of schoolchildren?

indicators.note: to enrol is to take in as a member, so the Scottish area takes the letter in

parts.note: the Borders is a region of southern Scotland

explanation.surface: A Scottish region signs up a party of pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: The Borders is the Scottish region next to England.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils who live in at a boarding school form a group called boarders.

clue.text: Old fogies fussing about south London district

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the abbreviation for south
fussing suggests agitated rearrangement, so the letters of old fogies are jumbled

explanation.surface: Elderly people fret over a district in south London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fussing' rearranges OLDFOGIES and 'about' wraps that around S. The Isle of Dogs is in east London, so 'south' is misleading as a location.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Dogs is a peninsula area of east London containing Canary Wharf.

clue.text: Kid succeeded on TV show

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
prog is a short form of programme

explanation.surface: A child won through on a television programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is British slang for a child.

clue.text: Identify him as Pete, in disguise

indicators.note: something in disguise has its appearance altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recognises that a man is Pete wearing a disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify with someone is to empathise, sharing their feelings.

clue.text: Like Cyrano de Bergerac, perhaps, showing size of nose?

definitions.meaning: the 1990 film of the play runs as a full-length cinema film
the nose is a facial feature, so its size is a measure of that feature

explanation.surface: Cyrano, famous for his huge nose, is described by its dimensions.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyrano de Bergerac is the play and film about a man with an enormous nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A full-length cinema film is called feature-length, and a nose is a facial feature.

clue.text: Competed in two rounds in Spanish city

indicators.note: the word for competed sits inside the two round letters

parts.note: O is a round letter, so two rounds give two Os
vied means competed

explanation.surface: Someone took part in two rounds of a contest held in a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oviedo is the capital of Asturias in northern Spain.

clue.text: Dog's left abandoned by person taking up residence

indicators.note: the letter for left is given up and dropped from the word

parts.note: a settler moves in to live somewhere new

explanation.surface: A dog is deserted by its owner moving into a new home.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': the dog is SETTLER with L ('left') 'abandoned'.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a breed of gundog, such as the Irish setter.

clue.text: Opportunist poet has a change of heart

indicators.note: the heart of the word, its central letter, is swapped for another

parts.note: Geoffrey Chaucer wrote The Canterbury Tales

explanation.surface: A self-serving poet changes his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has a change of heart' swaps the middle letter U of CHAUCER for N.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancer is British slang for someone who takes risks to grab advantage.

clue.text: Remembering job as baby-sitter?

parts.note: a calling is a vocation or profession
a baby-sitter's task is to mind the children

explanation.surface: Thinking back to work as a child-minder.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something to mind means recalling it to memory.

clue.text: Key player is apt to become animated about turning in

indicators.note: the mixed letters go around the turned word
becoming animated means getting stirred up, so the letters are mixed
the little word in is read backwards

explanation.surface: A keyboard musician tends to get excited when spinning round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become animated' rearranges ISAPT, which goes 'about' NI ('in' with 'turning').
explanation.definitionFit: A pianist plays the keys of a piano, hence a player of keys.

clue.text: Visible warning in view round shop

indicators.note: the word for view goes round the word for shop

parts.note: a sight is something seen, a view
a deli is a delicatessen, a kind of shop

explanation.surface: A warning sign can be seen in the view around a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelight is a small lamp on a vehicle that signals its presence to others.

clue.text: Excessive amount owed by first French cardinal

indicators.note: by means beside, placing the debt next to the French number

parts.note: un is French for one, the first cardinal number
what is due is owed

explanation.surface: A French cardinal of the Church owes too much money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a churchman, but here it is a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means more than is warranted, so excessive.

clue.text: One involved in shady arms-dealing, pushed to the edge?

indicators.note: the numeral is wrapped up within the jumble
shady suggests dodgy dealing, so the letters of arms-dealing are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone mixed up in illicit gun-running is forced out to the fringe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shady' rearranges ARMSDEALING and I ('One') is 'involved in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being marginalised means being pushed to the margins of society, literally its edge.

clue.text: Avoiding port, perhaps, sailor's given home in temporary shelter

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor, with the possessive giving S

indicators.note: the word for home sits inside the word for temporary shelter

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A sailor stays at home in a tent and keeps away from the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Port here is the fortified wine, not a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstinent person refrains from alcohol, such as port wine.

clue.text: I remain groggy at first, suffering terrible pain

indicators.note: suffering hints at being in a bad way, so the letters are disordered
the opening letter of groggy is taken

explanation.surface: A sufferer says they are still groggy at the start of a bout of pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges IREMAIN plus G, the first letter of 'groggy' ('at first').
explanation.definitionFit: A migraine is a severe recurring headache, a terrible pain.

clue.text: Fired up during fight, used dagger

indicators.note: during places the reversed word within the fight

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or scuffle

indicators.note: in a down entry up means read backwards

parts.note: lit means set on fire

explanation.surface: Inflamed in a brawl, someone pulled a dagger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LIT into TIL, which goes 'during' SET-TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a slim tapering blade.

clue.text: Mostly determined to follow urges and order a snack

indicators.note: the next pieces come after the word for urges

parts.note: to egg on is to urge

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is used, so its last letter goes

parts.note: bent on something means determined to do it
an edict is an official order

explanation.surface: Someone keen to satisfy cravings orders a light meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the T of BENT, leaving BEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs Benedict is a dish of poached eggs and hollandaise on muffins, a brunch snack.

clue.text: Finish off the whisky

definitions.meaning: to ... a plan is to put an end to it

explanation.surface: Someone polishes off the last of the whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch means to quash or end something, and is also the whisky of Scotland.

clue.text: One constantly criticising a marksman?

definitions.meaning: to snipe is to make sly critical remarks
a sharpshooter who fires from hiding

explanation.surface: A carping critic is likened to a sharpshooter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper is a hidden marksman, and one who snipes keeps making petty criticisms.

clue.text: Block two different swindles

parts.note: a con is a swindle
to do someone is to swindle them

explanation.surface: Two separate frauds are stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Block' looks like a verb meaning stop, but is a block of flats.
explanation.definitionFit: A condo, short for condominium, is an apartment block or flat in one.

clue.text: President's address during summer month by the river

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
Aug is the abbreviation for August
the Ural is a river in Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A president makes a speech in August beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A US president's inaugural is the address given on taking office.

clue.text: In room, child turned out light

indicators.note: the child is evicted, removed from the room

parts.note: a chamber is a room

explanation.surface: A child in a room switched off the light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out light' reads as switching off a lamp; 'turned out' actually removes CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is the middle colour of a traffic light.

clue.text: Joint league leaders?

definitions.meaning: a cut of beef for roasting
the team at the top of the table

explanation.surface: Two clubs share first place in the league.
explanation.definitionFit: Topside is a lean joint of beef, and the side at the top leads the league.

clue.text: Adherent of religion is seen in a hat, going after bishop

indicators.note: the hat piece comes after the bishop's letter

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: the word is goes inside a hat

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A believer is spotted wearing a hat behind a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' and 'going after' read as a sighting behind a cleric, but they are the container and order signals; Baha'i is a faith founded in Persia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bahaist is a follower of the Baha'i faith founded in nineteenth-century Persia.

clue.text: Present tense used in journal passed down through generations

parts.note: here means present, as in a roll call

indicators.note: the letter for tense is placed inside the journal

parts.note: a diary is a journal
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A present-tense diary entry gets handed down the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present tense' looks like grammar, but splits into HERE and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereditary traits or titles are inherited, passed from parent to child.

clue.text: Tape sent to recording studio in protest

definitions.meaning: a sample recording sent to a record company
a march or rally of protest

explanation.surface: A musician posts a tape to a studio as a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is a sample recording and also short for demonstration, a protest.
